sourcedFrom: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 (2024)
cleanIntro: The Commander-Style is the 4.25-inch SR1911 and Ruger publishes no separate book for it — the SR1911 manual names it by that designation on p.49. This guide walks the standard barrel with bushing; confirm the muzzle end of your slide at step one before going any further.

steps.title: Check your barrel before anything else
steps.action: Look at the muzzle end of the slide. If a separate barrel bushing ring surrounds the barrel and can be turned with the supplied wrench, this guide is yours. If the barrel comes out of the slide with no bushing around it, stop here — that is a bull barrel and this manual publishes a different procedure for it.
steps.prose: Ruger puts this at the head of the disassembly section rather than burying it, because three SR1911 strips live in one book and the wrong one will not come apart.
steps.quote: Disassembly and reassembly instructions vary depending upon the particular model of SR1911
steps.cite: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 — Disassembly/Reassembly, note, p.23
steps.warn: Be sure you are following the correct instructions for your firearm.

steps.title: Magazine out, fingers clear
steps.action: Keep the pistol pointed in a safe direction with your fingers outside the trigger guard, press the magazine catch and draw the magazine out of the butt.
steps.prose: Grip and muzzle discipline first — the pistol is not clear yet.
steps.quote: Keep the pistol pointed in a safe direction and keep your fingers outside of the trigger guard. Press the magazine catch and withdraw the magazine from the butt of the pistol.
steps.cite: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 — To Disassemble: Standard Barrel With Bushing, step 1, p.24
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly, or assembly.

steps.title: Lock it open and look twice
steps.action: Pull the slide back and lock it open by pressing up on the rear of the slide stop, then look into the chamber and at the breech face and confirm both are empty.
steps.prose: Ruger asks for the breech face as well as the chamber — a case can sit on the face after a failed ejection and never reach the chamber at all.
steps.quote: Pull the slide to the rear and lock it open by pressing upward on the rear end of the slide stop. Check the chamber and breech face to verify that the pistol is completely unloaded.
steps.cite: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 — To Disassemble: Standard Barrel With Bushing, step 2, p.24

steps.title: Bushing wrench on, quarter turn clockwise
steps.action: Let the slide run forward. Hold the pistol firmly, put the supplied wrench over the bushing, depress the recoil spring retainer and turn the wrench and bushing clockwise about a quarter turn until the plug and spring are free.
steps.prose: The wrench is doing two jobs at once — holding the plug captive and turning the bushing. Let either go and the plug leaves at speed.
steps.caution: THE RECOIL SPRING IS UNDER PRESSURE. YOU MUST CONTROL THE SPRING AND PLUNGER TO PREVENT IT FROM FLYING OUT AND CAUSING INJURY.
steps.quote: Turn the wrench and barrel bushing clockwise, approximately ¼ turn until the recoil spring plug and recoil spring are free.
steps.cite: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 — To Disassemble: Standard Barrel With Bushing, step 4, p.24

steps.title: Retainer and spring out, then cock the hammer
steps.action: Draw the recoil spring retainer and spring out of the front of the slide, then cock the hammer fully.
steps.prose: The hammer has to be back before the slide can pass over it. A slide that binds halfway off is usually a hammer that was left down.
steps.quote: Pull out the recoil retainer and spring (see Figure 11).
steps.cite: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 — To Disassemble: Standard Barrel With Bushing, steps 5 and 6, p.25

steps.title: Line the takedown notch up with the slide stop
steps.action: Press the slide rearward and walk it back until the takedown notch cut into the left side of the slide sits over the rear portion of the slide stop.
steps.prose: This is an exact alignment, not an approximate one — the stop only clears through that notch, and forcing it marks the slide.
steps.quote: Apply rearward pressure on the slide and move it back until the takedown notch in the left side of the slide is aligned with the rear portion of the slide stop as shown in Figure 12.
steps.cite: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 — To Disassemble: Standard Barrel With Bushing, step 7, p.25

steps.title: Slide stop out, slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Press inward on the slide stop pin from the opposite side of the frame and lift the slide stop clear, then hold the pistol so the grip safety is not squeezed and run the slide forward off the frame.
steps.prose: Ruger is specific about the grip safety — hold the pistol so it stays out, or the slide fouls on its way off.
steps.quote: Position your hands so that the grip safety is not activated and move the slide forward off of the frame.
steps.cite: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 — To Disassemble: Standard Barrel With Bushing, steps 8 and 9, p.25

steps.title: Guide rod out with the link up
steps.action: Turn the slide bottom up, rotate the barrel link into the up position for clearance, and move the recoil spring guide rod up and away from the barrel towards the rear of the slide.
steps.prose: The link position is what makes the room. Lever the rod out against a forward link and the link is what bends.
steps.quote: Rotate the barrel link into the “up” position to give the guide rod adequate clearance for removal.
steps.cite: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 — To Disassemble: Standard Barrel With Bushing, step 10, p.26

steps.title: Bushing out the front
steps.action: Rotate the barrel bushing counterclockwise until its lug lines up with the opening between the barrel hole and the recoil spring hole, then pull the bushing out of the front of the slide.
steps.prose: The lug has exactly one exit. Turn until it finds the gap rather than pulling against it.
steps.quote: Rotate the barrel bushing counterclockwise until the bushing lug is aligned with the opening between the barrel and recoil spring holes.
steps.cite: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 — To Disassemble: Standard Barrel With Bushing, step 11, p.26

steps.title: Barrel forward and out
steps.action: Rotate the barrel link to the forward position and draw the barrel out through the front of the slide. That is the field strip.
steps.prose: Slide, frame, barrel, bushing, recoil spring, plug and guide rod. Nothing further comes apart for cleaning.
steps.caution: DO NOT DRY FIRE YOUR RUGER® SR1911® PISTOL WHILE THE SLIDE IS REMOVED.
steps.quote: Rotate the barrel link to the forward position and remove the barrel through the front of the slide.
steps.cite: Ruger SR1911 Pistol Instruction Manual — FF 9/2024 R17 — To Disassemble: Standard Barrel With Bushing, step 12, p.26

deepAbsentReason: The SR1911 manual stops at the field strip and says so at the head of every one of its three disassembly procedures: "FOR ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, IT IS UNNECESSARY TO DISASSEMBLE THE FIREARM BEYOND WHAT IS DESCRIBED IN THESE INSTRUCTIONS. ANY FURTHER DISASSEMBLY SHOULD BE PERFORMED BY A LICENSED GUNSMITH." (p.24). Nothing past the strip is published, so this listing has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent-wet patch through the bore, then a correctly sized bristle brush the full length, then dry patches until they come out clean
Grease in the chamber interferes with feeding — clear it, then examine the bore against the light

cleaning.name: SLIDE & BARREL
tasks: Scrub powder residue off the breech face and around the extractor
Wipe the barrel hood, the locking lugs and the link
Lubricate the barrel locating ridge inside the barrel bushing, where the barrel contacts it

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: A drop of lubricant along each slide rail — the lower protruding rail is the surface that rides on the frame, not the groove in the slide
Lubricate the disconnector where it passes through the frame; light oil only

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: After any soak, shake the magazine out with the loading opening away from you — solvent left inside can kill a primer
Check follower movement and spring tension before the magazine goes back into service

reassembly: Turn the slide bottom up, turn the barrel link forward and place the barrel into the slide from the front, then insert the bushing and rotate it clockwise to lock it in place.
Fit the guide rod, run the slide onto the frame, align the takedown notch and press the slide stop home from the left.
Refit the recoil spring and plug and turn the bushing back counterclockwise with the wrench, keeping the plug controlled throughout.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty, check that the manual safety blocks the trigger, that the grip safety has to be squeezed before the trigger will release the hammer, and that the slide runs freely — pointed in a safe direction throughout.
